title: Grand Theft Auto 2/Gameplay
text:
GTA2 has the same top-down view of the original Grand Theft Auto, as well as its hijacking of vehicles and answering of phones. The player explores multi-level city districts on foot or in vehicles, earning money by committing crimes until you have the Target Score for that district, allowing you to leave the area and start play in the next one. Completing jobs for gangs earns more toward this target than other methods, but isn't necessary to complete the game.

Main menu
thumb|Main menu (Windows)
After opening the game, any input can skip to the main menu. However, if there's no input for a minute then a short gameplay movie plays until it ends, or any input is made, returning to the main menu.

The following can be selected from the right when highlighted red: 

 Play
 Options
 Quit

Select Quit to roll credits for the game, its music and the GTA2 . Any input will stop to quit the game.

Options
thumb|GTA2 Manager Video tab (Windows)
Selecting Options from the main menu will open the GTA2 Manager on Windows. The five tabs across the top allow you to customize settings for the game.

 Welcome: Language can be changed by selecting the corresponding flag, and Text Speed using a horizontal slider, from 1 (slowest) to 5 (fastest).
 Video:
 Frame Rate Control allows Frame Rate Limiter to be disabled or enabled.
 Lighting allows Noon or Dusk to be selected.
 Gamma Value can be changed using a vertical slider, from 0 to 30.
 Display Options allow Exploding Scores and Play Movie to be disabled or enabled.
 Screen Mode includes Direct3D and Primary Display Driver, and allows resolution to be selected.
 Display Mode allows Windows or Full Screen to be selected (640 x 480 minimum).
 Having Video problems? allows Special Recognition to be disabled or enabled.
 Audio: Effects and Music Volume can be changed using two vertical sliders, and disable or enable 3D Sound.
 Controls
 Network

Play
thumb|Play (Windows)
Selecting Play brings up the following four options:
 Player
 Resume Saved Status
 View High Scores
 Start Play

Select  to scroll right and left through PLAYER 0-7 (eight in total). Edit and enter any name after typing (8 characters maximum) or delete, selecting Yeah! or No way! when asked, Are you sure? If the player name isn't edited and entered, then any High Score is attributed to Empty when viewed, but deleting a name doesn't delete any saved status for that player.

Start Play in ../Area 1/, or if the player has unlocked other areas, scroll right and left to select a different area. Play starts with a top-down view of the player standing outside the Church. In Area 1, there's a phone ringing nearby to the upper left, which you can approach to answer, starting the .

Otherwise, colored arrow markers point to the public blue phone in each gang's territory, at least while there's still a job to be completed for that gang. Once in a gang's territory, these can be replaced by others pointing to any of that gang's phones with at least one job to offer to those who answer it if they have enough respect, the color of the notch of each arrow showing the phone's color. After answering a phone and starting a job, a big pink marker points in the direction of your target. This arrow also appears when your character is hidden from view, pointing in the direction you're facing.

When you enter an area, its name appears briefly in the top center of the screen, which can be displayed again. Other than these markers and names, there's no map in the game itself to aid navigation. In a gang's territory, its members, cars and signs can be seen. Civilians walking and driving the streets are normally left alone by these gangs, but if targeted by muggers (red tops) or hijackers (green tops) then gang members, and any cops, can attack those commiting crimes.

You can remain on foot to explore the city's districts, and it's sometimes recommended or even required to use stairs, cross footbridges or jump from roof to roof, but their sheer size encourages the use of vehicles, either by taking those parked or hijacking those driven, listening to the radio while traveling from place to place.

If you're ever reduced to 0  by anything other than being busted by cops, then Wasted! appears briefly in the center of the screen. Once wasted, you're released outside a nearby hospital at maximum Health again, but without any weapons,  or power-ups other than any .

You also lose a life: you start play in any new area with x5 and can earn more by passing ../Kill Frenzies/, or pick up more in Areas 2-3. However, once you're down to your last life, if you're wasted again then it's Game Over! You are Dead! and R.I.P. replace Player Quit! at the top of a summary of your criminal activity in that area, below its top three high scores:

 Vehicles hijacked
 Auto damage cost

 Civilians run down
 Civilians murdered

 Lawmen killed
 Gang members killed

 Fugitive factor

You can then choose from the following:

 Resume Saved Status
 Replay Previous Area 
 Back to Main Menu

Save
right
Resume Saved Status is grayed out and cannot be selected from the Play menu if the selected player has never saved status after starting play. Save status by entering the Church above where you start play, moving under the flashing Jesus Saves sign. It costs $50,000 to save, and you must not be on a job. When you successfully save on Windows, you can hear a voice proclaim "Hallelujah! Another soul saved!".

However, if you're on a job or have less then $50,000, you won't be able to save, and on Windows you'll hear the voice proclaim "Damnation! No donation, no salvation!"

You always start play outside this Church. Saving will store your score, jobs passed, ../Kill Frenzies/ passed and failed, ../Tokens/ collected, respect, Wanted level, Bonus Multiplier, lives, health and weapons. Everything else resets when you resume saved status.

right
If you ever lose track of the Church's location, look for any TV  driving the streets: the satellite dish on its roof points toward the Jesus Saves sign. You can simply travel in the direction indicated by the satellite dish, or hijack the TV Van itself and drive it to the Church: you hear organ music once nearby.

Once you have the Target Score, if you're not on a job then a big pink marker flashes and points toward the Church where, as well as saving status, you can now leave the area to start play in the next, or complete the game.

Score
Score is shown in the top right corner, and it's based on money earned by committing crimes. Once you have the Target Score, you can leave the area and start play in the next. This is most easily achieved by completing jobs for gangs, both because of the bonus earned and it increasing your Bonus Multiplier by 1.

Bonus Multiplier is the red number left of the Score, and you start play with minimum x1. In Areas 2-3, it can also be increased by 1 by picking up its power-up.

Bonus Multiplier is halved if busted without a , rounded down. This means x3 becomes x1, the minimum.

So avoid getting busted to maintain your Bonus Multiplier, as just completing all six green phone jobs in Area 1 (two for each gang) already has a significant impact:

That's 3.5 times more. Completing your first yellow phone job now earns $280,000 ($40,000 x 7), and your second $320,000 ($40,000 x 8): those eight bonuses alone can give you the Target Score for Area 1 ($1,000,000).

Bonus Multiplier doesn't affect the cost of saving status or using a garage, but it does affect money taken when mugged (-20 * (1-5), or -100 maximum in total before being multiplied).

However, Bonus Multiplier also affects bonuses earned committing any crimes, both on and off a job. Bonus for hijacking is based on the vehicle, while destroying the same vehicle earns bonus x5 (although not all vehicles that can be destroyed can also be hijacked).

Hijack a  (Area 1) or  (Areas 2-3), and if you remain stationary then a passing pedestrian can enter, becoming a passenger paying $1 per second. If you remain stationary or stop for five seconds, then any passenger exits.

Auto damage can be inflicted by colliding with another vehicle without destroying it, any bonus based on the impact of that collision (and running over a vehicle with a  counts as a series of high-impact collisions). Vehicles can also be damaged by attacking them with a weapon, although the bonus is only $1 per hit, regardless of damage inflicted: this means that if a  doesn't destroy a vehicle, the bonus is the same as hitting it with a single  bullet, even though the rocket can inflict up to 40 times more damage. However, this hit bonus isn't earned if the hit destroys the vehicle (and there's no bonus if it's driven or dropped into water).

Bonuses can also be earned for running down or killing civilians, lawmen and gang members:

So killing with a weapon rather than running down with a vehicle normally earns bonus x2, unless the pedestrian is a gang member (x2.5) or an Elvis impersonator.

Irony bonus x10 is earned if after hijacking a vehicle, you use it to run down its former driver (normally by turning right while going backward, while that driver is still on the ground).

This doesn't affect law enforcement or military vehicles which cannot be hijacked: any drivers are treated as pedestrians once they exit their vehicles.

Destroying vehicles, or running down or killing pedestrians, in quick succession earns bonus x1-5. For example, running down six Elvis impersonators slowly one-by-one can earn just $600 ($100 * 6), but do it quickly enough and the bonus is $2,000:

The following bonuses can also be earned in an Area:

Elvis Has Left the Building! is an additional bonus to that earned by killing six pedestrians in quick succession, so $32,000 ($2,000 + $30,000) is earned in total. The same is true of other bonuses, like Expeditious Execution!

Committing all these crimes makes you wanted, and remaining at level > 3 (4-6) without being busted or wasted earns $1 per second.

thumb|View High Scores (Windows)
Select View High Scores from the Play menu for the top five high scores for every Area (1-3) and Bonus Stage (A-I), scrolling right and left. All high scores can be viewed even if the area hasn't been unlocked yet. Default high scores are all the same, and those for every Area (1-3) will be easily beaten simply by completing the game.

Wanted
Committing crimes can earn points which can raise your Wanted level with the cops: 

Killing and destroying vehicles add points even when unseen by cops, but other crimes have to be seen to do so: you can fire a weapon or hijack a vehicle without adding points if unseen, but doing either with cops present triggers Wanted level 1.

There are also crimes which won't add points even when seen by cops, like traffic violations: you can speed through a red light in a stolen vehicle, alarm blaring and headlights flashing, driving the wrong way down the street and have a high-speed head-on collision with another vehicle, and cops aren't triggered even when present. You can even get away with bumping into a Cop Car, as long as you don't hit it with enough force to trigger Wanted level 1.

No response is triggered until you have enough points to trigger Wanted level 1, and this response changes if points increase beyond certain thresholds:

Any icons shown in the top center of the screen bob up and down if your location is known, otherwise they remain stationary.

File:GTA2 Icon Wanted.png

First, a single Cop Car, and a foot patrol in Areas 2-3, can chase you. Any Cop Car doesn't try to overtake any vehicle, but only the  and  are slightly faster, so any pursuit can be difficult to lose: try using traffic or other obstructions, or use s. Otherwise, you can slow down and stop, allowing the Cop Car to catch up until it also stops and two cops exit, approach your vehicle, open its door and drag you out: rather than let this happen, drive away and  the cops have to return to their car to continue the chase, by which time you can be long gone.

Any cops on foot are slower than you, so they can be outrun. Once none are on screen and your location is unknown, if you don't commit any more crimes and remain undetected long enough then they lose interest and your Wanted level is cleared.

If any cops get near enough then they try to arrest you, beating you until you have 0  and Busted! displays briefly in the center of the screen. Cops only draw pistols and fire when you're driving away in a vehicle, but they don't drop anything if killed.

Once busted, you're released outside a nearby police station at maximum Health again, but any weapons are confiscated and your Bonus Multiplier is halved, rounded down (although having a  when busted prevents this). However, if you're run over by a vehicle after being busted, then you're wasted outside that station before being discharged outside a nearby hospital.

File:GTA2 Icon Wanted.pngFile:GTA2 Icon Wanted.png

A second Cop Car can join the chase, but now they'll try to overtake and stop you by driving in front. Cops also have twice the Health, but they're still slower and can be outrun. However, even once none are on screen and your location is unknown, they won't lose interest and your Wanted level won't be cleared, no matter how long you remain undetected without further crime. Wanted level can now only be cleared by one of the following:

 Driving a vehicle through Max Paynt, to change its plates or respray
 Picking up a 
 Passing a job or Kill Frenzy
 Being busted or wasted

File:GTA2 Icon Wanted.pngFile:GTA2 Icon Wanted.pngFile:GTA2 Icon Wanted.png

Roadblocks can now be set up, manned by cops with twice the Health, who draw pistols and fire on any vehicle, but won't approach unless you're on foot. From now on, all those who spawn are now as fast as you are, so if they're right behind you then it can be difficult to turn and fire without getting busted: however, they don't jump over vehicles, so you can do so to widen the gap between you as they go around, or try dropping  as you run forward so that they land behind you, killing those chasing.

File:GTA2 Icon Wanted.pngFile:GTA2 Icon Wanted.pngFile:GTA2 Icon Wanted.pngFile:GTA2 Icon Wanted.png

This is the maximum Wanted level in ../Area 1/, and from now on $1 (x Multiplier) is earned per second while Wanted. A SWAT Van can now join the chase, trying to ovetake and stop you by driving in front. Once it catches up, four SWAT officers armed with s can exit, just as fast as you and with twice the Health of the cops manning any roadblocks. However, while SWAT officers may approach your vehicle, open its door and drag you out, they've no interest in busting you and they'll keep shooting until you're wasted. Since they have the highest Health of any pedestrian, picking up and using a  is recommended.

File:GTA2 Icon Wanted.pngFile:GTA2 Icon Wanted.pngFile:GTA2 Icon Wanted.pngFile:GTA2 Icon Wanted.pngFile:GTA2 Icon Wanted.png

This is normally the maximum Wanted level in ../Area 2/, at which point no new Cop Cars or SWAT Vans appear and the cops are replaced by special agents and their cars. Agents manning any roadblocks use s and have the same Health as the cops they replaced but will shoot instead of approaching you, while Special Agent Cars driven on the streets have two agents, one with a Silenced S-Uzi and the other a , both with 25% more Health than those manning roadblocks: while they may approach your vehicle, open its door and drag you out, like the SWAT team this is only to shoot and waste you.

File:GTA2 Icon Wanted.pngFile:GTA2 Icon Wanted.pngFile:GTA2 Icon Wanted.pngFile:GTA2 Icon Wanted.pngFile:GTA2 Icon Wanted.png

This is the maximum Wanted level in ../Area 3/, at which point martial law is declared: it's only triggered in Area 2 when the Tank leaves the Army Base during the Redneck  job. Civilians on the streets are replaced by soldiers, who have no more Health but are armed with s, which given their numbers can be extremely dangerous, particularly since they normally fire on vehicles, only approaching, opening the door and dragging you out when you're in a , and only then so they can waste you. Special Agent Cars and civilian vehicles are also replaced by the military, as not just Tanks but (Armed) s and s patrol. Roadblocks are unmanned but made with Tanks, which do not move and cannot be hijacked, but whose turrets can turn to aim and fire their s.

Health equals the number of S-Uzi bullets required to kill:

Soldiers in the Area 2 Army Base have twice as much Health as those walking the streets, but bonuses are the same as for running down or killing normal civilians.
